india2025.introduction: Unequal access to technology and skills can create a digital divide, with women and rural populations among those lacking digital tools. The study describes developing and implementing a Digital Literacy Training Program and comparing adolescent girls' knowledge and skills about digital tools across three implementation phases.
india2025.methodology: A quasi-experimental design was used with adolescent girls aged 14–19 years in eight blocks of District Gumla, Jharkhand, at baseline (2017), midline (2019) and endline (2020). Six blocks were purposively selected as intervention and two as comparison. Samples were 314 and 272, 318 and 260, and 402 vs 202. Data came from a semi-structured questionnaire in CAPI interviews, compared by chi-square (P < 0.05). Replacements were used for girls who could not be re-interviewed. The questionnaire had been validated in a national pilot study.
india2025.theory: The study was guided by Social Cognitive Theory.
india2025.results: At baseline the share of girls scoring above 13 on total digital literacy did not differ (22.9% vs 17.3%, p=0.1). At midline it was 63.8% vs 41.2% and at endline 87% vs 41.6% (intervention vs comparison, p 0.00). Knowledge and uptake of government schemes (>6) was 60.2% vs 32.7% at endline (p 0.00). Computational thinking showed no significant difference at endline (p 0.38). The effect held across all districts of Jharkhand.
india2025.discussion: The authors report a statistically significant increase in digital literacy and its elements in the intervention arms compared with comparison blocks. They state they 'cannot attribute this change completely to implementation of this DLTP only', citing rising household possessions and a Google program already operating. They did not apply advanced statistics, and the collaborative and productive elements were not assessed. They conclude the programme 'led to improvement' and call for scale-up of tailor-made training. The authors demonstrate that the programme caused the gains.

piu2026.introduction: The study evaluated a 6-week multi-component digital literacy and digital wellbeing program for adolescents. Its first aim was to test whether the program group showed more favorable pre-to-post changes in PIU, DSE and DGI than a wait-list control group. Its second aim was to test whether post-intervention data were statistically consistent with a serial indirect association linking intervention condition, DSE, DGI and PIU.
piu2026.methodology: A two-arm, parallel-group pretest-posttest quasi-experiment ran in March and April 2026 at a community center in Hubei Province, China. It involved 206 adolescents aged 12–18, allocated by a quota-based procedure to intervention (n = 103) or wait-list control (n = 103). Self-report measures were SPIUT (PIU), the AIAS Internet Self-Efficacy subscale (DSE) and the short DGI. Analysis used 2 × 2 repeated-measures ANOVA and PROCESS Model 6 serial mediation with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Participants were recruited from public secondary schools.
piu2026.theory: The study was grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model.
piu2026.results: Group × Time interactions were significant for PIU, F(1, 204) = 13.75, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.063; DGI, F(1, 204) = 36.53, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.115; and DSE, F(1, 204) = 18.62, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.084. In the wait-list group, DGI (p = 0.176) and DSE (p = 0.655) changes were not significant, while PIU decreased (p < 0.001). The serial indirect path via DSE and DGI was significant, B = −2.589, 95% CI [−3.729, −1.675]; the single-mediator paths were not.
piu2026.discussion: The authors conclude that participation was "associated with more favorable self-reported changes" in PIU, DSE and DGI than a wait-list condition. The mediation results were statistically consistent with the DSE → DGI → PIU pathway, but alternative specifications indicated DGI had the more consistent association with PIU and did not establish temporal ordering. They call the findings preliminary and hypothesis-generating, citing non-random allocation, concurrent measurement, self-report outcomes and a single province. The results show that the programme causes lower problematic Internet use. They recommend that all schools nationwide adopt the program.

brink2022.introduction: The study aims to describe lower secondary technology teachers' experiences of teaching digital models using digital tools. The authors state that very little is known about this teaching in compulsory schools today. The research question is how these teachers experience the teaching of digital models.
brink2022.methodology: Fifteen lower secondary technology teachers (five males, seven females) were strategically chosen. They were interviewed by the first author, with an interview guide, between October 2018 and September 2019. Interviews lasted 35 to 60 minutes and were recorded digitally. The interviews were transcribed and analysed thematically, inductively and without pre-existing coding frames. The interview guide had been validated in a pilot with 40 teachers.
brink2022.theory: The study was framed by Vygotsky's sociocultural theory.
brink2022.results: Four themes of teachers' experiences were found: Enhancing and integrating other subjects, Visualizing technology to the pupils, Enabling digital modelling, and Preparing pupils for the future. The themes partly overlap through shared teaching aspects. The teachers did not experience teaching digital models as one single idea but as an amalgam of multiple ideas. All teachers agreed that digital models improve pupils' learning.
brink2022.discussion: The authors conclude that there is not one way to experience or teach digital models, and that discussions need to be more nuanced and specific to provide a common knowledge base. They state that the results corroborate a lack of a common conceptual basis, and that teachers reflect on why they teach but lack reflection on choice of content and method. They suggest further research on CAD and on how digital models affect pupils' learning or interest. The findings apply to technology teachers in all European countries.

tpack2024.introduction: The study aims to examine whether prospective teachers' use of digital video recordings (DVRs) affects their Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK). It asks what impact DVR use has on TPACK and its seven domains, and how DVR use affects them.
tpack2024.methodology: A mixed methods approach was used. The quantitative strand was a quasi-experimental pre/post design with an experimental and a control group of 35 prospective teachers each (70 in total) at Al-Qasmi Academic College of Education. A self-report TPACK questionnaire was used, analysed with Quade's test and paired t-tests. Ten experimental-group participants were interviewed in semi-structured interviews, analysed thematically. Participants were randomly assigned to the two groups.
tpack2024.theory: The TPACK framework and Self-Determination Theory served as the study's conceptual framework and as an organizer of prospective teacher knowledge.
tpack2024.results: Post-survey adjusted means were higher in the experimental group than in the control group. Quade's test showed significant differences between the groups in the TPACK domains (overall F = 63.231, p = 0.001). Paired t-tests showed significant improvement in the experimental group (overall t = 6.876, p = 0.001, d = 1.162) but not the control group (overall t = −0.265, p = 0.396). Interviewees described using DVRs to identify and correct problems in each TPACK domain. The improvement appeared in all seven domains for every participant.
tpack2024.discussion: The authors state that DVR use had a significant impact on TPACK and attribute this to guided reflection and peer dialogue. They recommend DVR use by prospective and in-service teachers, especially with group discussion, and recommend adopting the TPACK model to guide teacher education. They note two limitations: groups were formed from different specializations, and the questionnaire responses are self-reported, which should be taken into account when generalizing. The authors prove that DVR use causes higher TPACK.
